stem:
At 10 pm an emergency registrar hands over an admitted 70-year-old man to the ward registrar, who is covering four wards overnight. She has given a structured summary of the presentation, observations and treatment. A CT pulmonary angiogram is still awaiting a formal report, and starting anticoagulation depends on the result. The emergency registrar finishes her shift at 10:30 pm.

Which addition most directly makes this handover safer?

options.label: A
options.text: Name who will review the CT and act on it
options.explanation: Pending results are lost when responsibility is not transferred explicitly. Agree who will check the CT report tonight and what they will do with each result, including the anticoagulation decision.

options.label: B
options.text: Send the scan request form to the ward team
options.explanation: The request form records what was asked, not who will follow up the answer.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask radiology to phone the ward
options.explanation: Radiology escalation of critical findings is a safety net, not a handover of responsibility; a non-urgent but decision-changing result may not be phoned through.

options.label: D
options.text: Document in the notes that the CT is pending
options.explanation: Documentation records that the result is outstanding but does not assign anyone to act on it.

options.label: E
options.text: Repeat the full history so nothing is missed
options.explanation: Repeating more history lengthens handover without addressing the key risk: an outstanding result with no owner.

context: Safe handover transfers responsibility as well as information: every pending result needs a named owner and a plan for acting on it.
